segments.title: Kure waterfront: JS Kaga and the Yamato Museum
segments.body: JS Kaga is visible in Kure harbour at the start of the update. Although the Yamato Museum is closed to the public, some of its exhibits can still be seen through the windows. The museum frontage is shaped like Yamato's bow, and walking along it conveys the battleship's length. Nearby, the JMSDF museum has a displayed submarine for visitors to explore. The view places Japan's imperial-era naval memory and the modern Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force on the same waterfront.

evidence.note: The speaker identifies Kaga, the Yamato Museum bow-inspired frontage, and the JMSDF museum submarine.

segments.summary: JS Kaga, the Yamato Museum's bow-shaped frontage, and the JMSDF museum submarine appear together on Kure's waterfront.

segments.title: Kure shipyard, harbour cruise, and command headquarters
segments.body: Kure's naval sites extend beyond the museum frontage. The next stops are a shipyard tour and a harbour cruise, which will show what is happening around the working port. The day's earlier visit included the former commander-in-chief headquarters room. The itinerary combines a surviving command space, museum displays, shipbuilding, and a view of the active harbour.

evidence.note: The speaker mentions a shipyard tour, harbour cruise, and the old commander-in-chief headquarters room.

segments.summary: The group prepares for a shipyard tour and harbour cruise after visiting Kure's former commander-in-chief headquarters room.
